input.rationale: Section 14.1 gives us a RevMed indemnity for (a) RevMed's negligence/recklessness/willful misconduct, (b) breach of its representations and warranties, and (c) breach of its obligations, with standard notice, control and cooperation procedure in Section 14.3, and Section 14.5 confirms the consequential-damages waiver does not cut back indemnities. However, it contains no head of indemnity for third-party claims that the licensed technology or the Products infringe or misappropriate third-party IP. That risk is only picked up indirectly through breach of the Article XIII IP warranties, most of which are knowledge-qualified and given only as of the Execution Date (p0549: "To RevMed's Knowledge... does not infringe"), while Section 14.2(a) affirmatively places third-party claims arising from our Research, Development, Manufacture and Commercialization of Products on us, and Section 10.7 only gives us a first right to negotiate a third-party licence at our own cost. Under the detection guidance this fails the fallback (Vendor indemnity excluding IP infringement), so we propose the minimal addition of an express IP infringement head as new Section 14.1(d), leaving RevMed's existing carve-outs for our own negligence and breaches intact. Our own indemnity in Section 14.2 is otherwise appropriately confined to our development/commercialization conduct and breaches.

proposal.summary: Add a RevMed third-party IP infringement indemnity to Section 14.1
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 14.1 covers only RevMed's misconduct and its breaches, so a third-party claim that the licensed technology or the Products infringe IP falls on us (and is even swept into our indemnity in Section 14.2(a)). We have added an express RevMed IP infringement indemnity, consistent with our playbook requirement that the licensor stand behind third-party IP claims relating to the technology it licenses; RevMed remains protected by the existing carve-outs for our own negligence and breaches.
